Chapter 5: Living Authentically by Aligning Values and Actions
Have you ever felt that quiet longing—the sense that, even when everything seems fine on the outside, something’s just missing underneath?
That feeling often comes from a gap between our values and our actions. It’s the space between who you want to be, and how you’re actually living each day. Now, authenticity isn’t about perfection or always having the right answer.
It’s really about closing that gap—making sure your daily choices line up with what matters most to you.
Picture this: someone who truly values creativity, but spends most days lost in routine tasks, never making time for art or play.
Over time, they start to feel restless, almost as if life is slipping by. It’s not that creativity has disappeared—it’s just been crowded out by the busyness and obligations of daily life.
The first real step toward authenticity is simply noticing when this disconnect happens. Ask yourself, what really matters to me? And then—am I making space for it?
To live authentically, you need honesty—with yourself and with others. That means admitting your desires, your fears, and even your limits, even when it makes you uncomfortable.
I think of a friend who spent years pretending to love their high-powered career, only to finally admit they craved a slower, simpler life.
The choice to step back and pursue work that actually felt meaningful was tough. There was confusion, even criticism from others. But the sense of relief? Unmistakable. It was like a weight had been lifted, opening up new possibilities.
Authenticity also means drawing boundaries—saying no to things that don’t line up with your values.
That’s not always easy, especially when it means letting others down or going against what’s expected. Maybe you value family, so you leave work early even if it means missing out on a promotion. Or you’re committed to honesty, and you risk conflict by speaking up when something feels off.
This isn’t a one-time fix. Our values change, life shifts, and new challenges keep coming.
Authenticity is a practice—a series of choices made in the direction of what feels true for you. On some days, the gap between your values and your actions feels huge. Other days, it’s barely there.
What matters is your willingness to keep asking what’s important, and keep choosing alignment over convenience.
Now, living authentically doesn’t promise an easy life. There are risks—failure, rejection, uncertainty.
But there’s also a deep sense of fulfillment, a feeling of being truly at home in your own skin.
Little by little, life becomes less about meeting everyone else’s expectations, and more about honoring what actually feels right for you.
